lessons.false_positive_guard: Only keys whose separator-insensitive normalized form equals a protected authority key are findings.
lessons.invariant: Metadata must never contradict or alias the authority contract.
lessons.repair_pattern: Normalize security-sensitive keys by case-folding and removing separators, then reject canonical and aliased authority keys recursively.
lessons.required_regression: Exercise camelCase, mixedCase, snake_case, hyphenated, spaced, and fully separator-split aliases at every metadata depth.
lessons.trigger: Untrusted metadata uses camel, mixed, hyphenated, spaced, or separator-split aliases of protected authority fields.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Canonical protected keys with the exact false value remain permitted only where the contract explicitly serializes them.
lessons.invariant: Protected non-authority fields remain exactly false after merging untrusted metadata.
lessons.repair_pattern: Reject protected keys before merge and reassert the immutable false authority envelope after sanitization.
lessons.required_regression: Attempt true, truthy, null, nested, and conflicting values for every protected field.
lessons.trigger: Caller metadata overwrites a protected false authority field or supplies a contradictory canonical value.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Computed internal values with a provable fixed-size representation are not treated as attacker-controlled variable evidence.
lessons.invariant: Every attacker-controlled retained evidence path needs count and byte bounds.
lessons.repair_pattern: Apply per-item, aggregate, and canonical serialized-byte ceilings before retention or handoff.
lessons.required_regression: Use few extremely large items as well as many small items and assert fail-closed behavior.
lessons.trigger: Attacker-controlled retained evidence has an item count cap but no per-item and aggregate byte caps.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Order-significant arrays remain valid when their contract explicitly defines order and digest semantics.
lessons.invariant: Canonical representation equality is checked before accepting an external digest.
lessons.repair_pattern: Validate structure, ordering, uniqueness, runtime semantics, canonical reconstruction, field equality, then canonical digest.
lessons.required_regression: Reorder and duplicate records/source refs, recompute a digest, and assert rejection.
lessons.trigger: Externally supplied records or set-like fields are unsorted/duplicated yet accepted with a self-consistent digest.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Do not flag order-significant sequences whose contract explicitly preserves order.
lessons.invariant: Canonicalize before ID assignment, digesting, caching, or interchange.
lessons.repair_pattern: Build a stable semantic sort key, deduplicate, then assign identities and compute digests.
lessons.required_regression: Permute equivalent records repeatedly and assert byte-identical canonical output and stable IDs.
lessons.trigger: Set-like records reach ID assignment, digesting, caching, or interchange in caller-provided order.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Streaming or priority queues are exempt only when priority ordering is explicit, deterministic, and tested.
lessons.repair_pattern: Normalize the full bounded candidate set, sort by a stable key, deduplicate, then truncate.
lessons.required_regression: Permute over-cap inputs and assert the same retained subset.
lessons.trigger: A cap is applied to a set-like collection before stable sorting.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Historical evidence may be retained when it is explicitly labeled historical and bound to its SHA.
lessons.invariant: Every verification claim binds to an exact commit, run, and observed status.
lessons.repair_pattern: Preserve exact evidence status vocabulary and repository-head binding in receipts and summaries.
lessons.required_regression: Reject configured→passed, historical→current, file-exists→executed, and manual→CI claim upgrades.
lessons.trigger: Configured, historical, queued, or unexecuted evidence is described as a current-head pass.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Identical frame conventions and explicitly converted changes are permitted.
lessons.invariant: Basis changes must be explicit and tested.
lessons.repair_pattern: Apply a declared conversion matrix/quaternion or reject mixed conventions fail closed.
lessons.required_regression: Cover handedness, up-axis, forward-axis, finite transforms, and round-trip tolerance.
lessons.trigger: Parent and child frames change handedness or axes without an explicit conversion.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Geometric scale remains allowed when separately represented from unit conversion.
lessons.invariant: Units are applied exactly once and remain conceptually distinct from geometric scale.
lessons.repair_pattern: Convert local translations once and keep absolute unit conversion out of accumulated geometric scale, or use parent-relative conversion.
lessons.required_regression: Compose root and child centimeter frames and assert 100 cm resolves to 1 m, not 0.01 m or 100 m.
lessons.trigger: Absolute unit scale is applied both to local translation and accumulated transform scale in nested non-meter frames.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Valid repository-relative POSIX paths with ordinary dots inside filenames remain allowed.
lessons.invariant: A path must be canonical before it becomes evidence.
lessons.repair_pattern: Require repository-relative canonical POSIX paths and construct anchors only from validated components.
lessons.required_regression: Reject absolute, traversal, dot-segment, repeated separator, backslash, control, and overlong paths.
lessons.trigger: A source anchor contains absolute, traversal, dot, repeated-slash, backslash, or control-character path aliases.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Documented runtime-only cross-field checks are valid when the interchange validator always executes them.
lessons.invariant: Schema and runtime must expose the same acceptance boundary, with runtime cross-field validation where JSON Schema cannot express it.
lessons.repair_pattern: Align field constraints, validate the meta-schema, and add explicit runtime semantic checks for cross-field invariants.
lessons.required_regression: Run positive and negative fixtures through both schema and runtime and compare outcomes.
lessons.trigger: Schema-valid data is rejected by runtime semantics or runtime accepts values the schema rejects.

lessons.false_positive_guard: A repository-wide discovery command may satisfy wiring when its inclusion is deterministic and explicitly tested.
lessons.invariant: A regression is evidence only when the intended workflow actually executes it.
lessons.repair_pattern: Wire the regression into compile, fatal lint, and focused pytest gates before claiming coverage.
lessons.required_regression: Assert the workflow text includes the test in every required stage.
lessons.trigger: A new regression test exists but is omitted from compile, lint, or focused test workflow lists.

lessons.false_positive_guard: Benign percent encoding that cannot introduce a separator or authority ambiguity is permitted.
lessons.invariant: URI normalization must not change path meaning after validation.
lessons.repair_pattern: Reject decoded separator changes and ambiguous URI forms instead of stripping or repairing them.
lessons.required_regression: Exercise %2f, %5c, repeated separators, credentials, queries, fragments, and dot segments.
lessons.trigger: A URI contains encoded separators, repeated separators, credentials, query, fragment, or backslash aliases.
